Decreased intake and unintentional weight loss are common
nutrition problems for many individuals with Parkinson’s dis-
ease.67 Tremors and fatigue can contribute to decreased intake,
as greater eﬀ ort is required to physically place the food in the
mouth. Th is extra eﬀ ort can increase fatigue at mealtimes, 
resulting in less intake. Weight loss can also occur despite 
maintaining consistent baseline caloric intake. Nutrition inter-
ventions should address the possible need for increased energy 
intake and close monitoring of weight status. Individuals expe-
